explanation: Copy the original matrix. For every destination cell, inspect its entire original row and column; write zero if either contained a zero. The snapshot prevents newly written zeros from triggering additional clearing.
timeComplexity: O(RC(R+C)) worst-case time: each of RC cells searches up to C entries of its snapshot row and R entries of its column, in addition to an O(RC) copy.
spaceComplexity: O(RC) auxiliary space for the deep row snapshot. This implementation does not meet the optional constant-space optimization goal.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Python algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: The contract clears cell (r,c) exactly when some original cell in row r or column c is zero. The snapshot preserves those original values, and the two searches test exactly that condition. Writes affect only existing cells, preserving the outer matrix and row identities.
walkthrough: For [[1,5,0],[6,7,8]], every cell in row 0 sees the original zero. Cell (1,2) sees it in column 2, while (1,0) and (1,1) see no original zero in their row or column. The final matrix is [[0,0,0],[6,7,0]]. The method returns no value; the wrapper displays the mutated input. The callable returns no value; expected records the original matrix after mutation, and the harness additionally checks row identity.
edgeCases: A matrix with no zeros is unchanged.
Multiple zeros may mark the same row or column.
Cells change in place while original row identities remain intact.
